requirements.source_text: The Supplier shall furnish the membrane filtration system, two band screens, and two circular primary clarifier mechanisms as specified.
The Supplier shall provide equipment design, fabrication, delivery to the site, installation supervision, startup, testing, and operator training.
Equipment shall be delivered to the site within 40 weeks after approval of the shop drawings.
requirements.parameter: delivery time after shop drawing approval

requirements.source_text: Shop drawings shall be submitted within 10 weeks after the notice of assignment.
The Supplier may propose packaged skids for the chemical cleaning equipment.
Proposals shall be delivered to the Town Clerk, 41 Harbor Street, Lakeview, in a sealed envelope marked with the RFP number.
Requests for approval of an equal product shall be received no later than 14 days before the proposal due date.
Questions about this Request for Proposals shall be submitted in writing to the Engineer.
The Supplier shall submit a list of at least three (3) installations of the proposed membrane system in municipal wastewater service, each in operation for not less than 2 years.
For each installation, provide the owner's name, a contact person, the design flow, and the date of startup on Form B.
The Supplier shall maintain a service center able to place a technician on site within 48 hours of a request.
The Supplier should identify the location of its nearest parts warehouse.
The Supplier shall conduct an on site pilot test of the proposed membrane system for not less than 90 days.
The pilot unit shall use full scale membrane modules of the type proposed.
The pilot shall demonstrate permeate total phosphorus not exceeding 0.1 mg/L for the final 30 days of operation.
The Supplier shall submit a pilot test report within 30 days after the end of pilot testing.
The cost of pilot testing shall be included in the proposal price.
The Supplier shall warrant all equipment against defects in materials and workmanship for 2 years from substantial completion.
The Supplier shall guarantee that the membrane system meets the effluent requirements of Section 46 61 00 for 1 year after startup.
If the guarantee is not met, the Supplier shall furnish additional equipment and labor at no cost to the Owner.
Proposal prices shall remain valid for 120 days after the proposal due date.
The selected Supplier shall furnish a performance bond in the amount of 100 percent of the contract price.
Liquidated damages of $1,500 per day shall be assessed for each day that equipment delivery is late.
All iron and steel, manufactured products, and construction materials shall comply with the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA).
The Supplier shall submit a BABA certification letter with the shop drawings.
Payment shall be made as follows: 90 percent on delivery and 10 percent on final acceptance.
The Supplier shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence.
The Supplier shall name the Owner and the Engineer as additional insureds on its liability policies.
The Supplier shall indemnify the Owner against claims arising from defects in the equipment.
Proposers should visit the existing plant before submitting a proposal.
The proposal shall include a completed Form A and a completed Form B.
The Supplier shall submit a submittal schedule within 14 days after the notice to proceed.
Allow 21 days for the Engineer's initial review of each submittal.
Submittals should be organized by specification paragraph.
Each submittal shall be transmitted electronically in PDF format with a transmittal form.
Each submittal shall include a cover sheet listing the project name, the specification Section, and the paragraph numbers covered.
Individual submittal files shall not exceed 50 MB.
Shop drawings shall be drawn to scale
shall show dimensions, materials, equipment weights, and anchor bolt locations
Product data shall be marked to show the specific model, options, and accessories proposed.
Manuals shall include equipment descriptions, operating procedures, lubrication schedules, troubleshooting guides, and a recommended spare parts list.
Operation and maintenance manuals shall be submitted in searchable PDF format no later than 30 days before startup.
Preliminary manuals shall be reviewed by the Engineer before the final manuals are prepared.
Resubmittals shall identify every change made since the previous submission.
Submit shop drawings for the band screens in accordance with Section 01 33 00.
Submit hydraulic calculations showing the headloss through each screen at peak hour flow with the screen 30 percent blinded.
Screens shall be the product of a manufacturer regularly engaged in producing band screens for municipal service.
The band screens shall be warranted against defects in materials and workmanship for 2 years from substantial completion.
Band screens shall be Brightwater Systems Model BS-300, or approved equal.
Each screen shall pass the peak hour flow of 5.0 MGD with the other screen out of service.
Headloss through a clean screen shall not exceed 6 inches at peak hour flow.
Screen frames, panels, and wetted parts shall be Type 316 stainless steel.
Anchor bolts and fasteners shall be Type 316 stainless steel.
Seals and brushes shall be resistant to grease, hydrogen sulfide, and chlorine.
Provide a spray wash system with a dedicated booster pump for each screen.
Each booster pump shall deliver not less than 40 gpm at 80 psi.
Spray nozzles should be of the quick disconnect type.
The screen should be arranged for future addition of a second wash water booster pump.
Provide one screenings washer compactor for each screen.
Washed and compacted screenings shall have a solids content of not less than 40 percent.
The washer compactor shall reduce the organic content of the screenings by not less than 80 percent.
Each screen shall be furnished with a NEMA 4X stainless steel local control panel.
The screen shall start automatically on high differential level and on an adjustable timer.
Provide a level sensor upstream and downstream of each screen to measure differential level.
Motors shall be premium efficiency, totally enclosed, and rated for 460 volts, 3 phase, 60 Hz.
Install the screens in accordance with the manufacturer's written instructions and the approved shop drawings.
After installation, each screen shall be operated for not less than 8 hours without malfunction.
The Supplier shall furnish a written field test report signed by the manufacturer's representative.
Provide a manufacturer's representative on site for not less than 4 days for installation inspection and startup of the screens.
Provide not less than 8 hours of operator training on the band screens.
Each clarifier shall be designed for a peak hour flow of 2.5 MGD.
Each clarifier shall be designed for a surface overflow rate not exceeding 2,500 gpd/sf at peak hour flow.
Submit drive torque calculations and structural calculations for the clarifier mechanisms, sealed by a professional engineer.
Submit the drive manufacturer's certification of the AGMA service factor.
The clarifier drives shall be warranted for 5 years from substantial completion.
Clarifier mechanisms, drives, and skimmers shall be furnished by a single manufacturer.
The drive shall have a continuous torque rating of not less than 45,000 ft-lb.
The drive shall be rated for a service life of not less than 20 years at continuous torque.
Drive motors shall be 1 hp, 460 volts, 3 phase, totally enclosed.
Provide a torque overload device that stops the drive motor at 120 percent of the continuous torque rating.
The torque overload device shall have a local torque indicator.
The clarifier drive should be furnished with a torque overload alarm contact.
Provide two collector arms with steel scraper blades and replaceable squeegees.
Scraper blades shall travel at a tip speed of not more than 10 feet per minute.
Provide a full radius skimmer that moves scum to a scum box at each revolution.
The skimmer should discharge to a scum box located outside the effluent launder.
Submerged steel shall be galvanized after fabrication in accordance with ASTM A123.
Anchor bolts, nuts, and washers for the mechanisms shall be Type 316 stainless steel.
Provide an energy dissipating influent well with a diameter of not less than 15 percent of the clarifier diameter.
Provide fiberglass density current baffles around the full perimeter.
Install the mechanisms under the supervision of the manufacturer's representative.
Grout the drive support to provide full bearing under the drive base.
Operate each mechanism in the dry for not less than 4 hours to show freedom from binding.
Operate each mechanism with water for not less than 24 hours and record the drive torque.
Provide a manufacturer's representative on site for not less than 3 days for installation inspection, startup, and training on the clarifier mechanisms.
The membrane system shall be designed to accept flow equalization basin return flows of up to 0.5 MGD without exceeding the design net flux.
Submit operation and maintenance manuals per Section 01 33 00.
Submit shop drawings showing the cassette arrangement, the piping and valve layouts, and the dimensions of each membrane tank.
Submit a process design report showing the flux, transmembrane pressure, and air scour demand at each design flow.
Submit the membrane manufacturer's written warranty.
Submit control system programming documentation, including control narratives and alarm lists, 60 days before factory testing.
The membrane modules shall be manufactured under a quality management system certified to ISO 9001.
The membrane system supplier shall have single source responsibility for the membrane modules, permeate pumps, blowers, and controls.
The membrane system control panel shall be listed under UL 508A.
Membrane modules shall be shipped in sealed containers with a preservative solution.
Store membrane modules indoors at temperatures between 40 and 95 degrees F.
Membrane modules shall not be allowed to dry out after wetting.
The membrane system, except the membrane modules, shall be warranted against defects in materials and workmanship for 2 years from substantial completion.
Warranty claims shall be answered within 5 working days.
The membrane system shall be furnished by the Supplier selected under the Request for Proposals.
Membranes shall be immersed hollow fiber or flat sheet membranes with a nominal pore size of 0.04 micron or smaller.
The membrane system shall produce effluent total phosphorus not exceeding 0.1 mg/L as a monthly average.

Permeate turbidity shall not exceed 0.2 NTU 95 percent of the time.
Permeate total suspended solids shall not exceed 1 mg/L.
Each cassette shall be removable from its tank without draining the other trains.
Cassette frames shall be Type 316 stainless steel.
Membrane cassettes should be interchangeable between trains.
Each cassette shall weigh not more than 4,000 pounds when lifted wet from the tank.
Membrane fibers shall be made of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) with an internal support.
Each module shall be tested for integrity at the factory before shipment.
Membranes shall tolerate a cumulative sodium hypochlorite exposure of not less than 500,000 ppm hours over the membrane life.
Provide one permeate pump for each train, plus one installed spare pump.
Each permeate pump shall deliver 1,160 gpm at peak hour flow with one train out of service.
The Supplier may furnish permeate pumps of either the end suction or the self priming type.
Permeate pumps shall be driven by variable frequency drives.
Permeate pumps shall be capable of reverse flow for backpulsing.
Provide one air scour blower for each train and one installed standby blower.
Blowers shall be rotary lobe or rotary screw type with sound enclosures.
Blower sound pressure level shall not exceed 80 dBA at 3 feet from the enclosure.
Provide a chemical cleaning system for maintenance and recovery cleaning with sodium hypochlorite and citric acid.
Chemical metering pumps shall be peristaltic hose pumps.
Each chemical storage tank shall hold not less than 30 days of chemical at design average conditions.
Provide secondary containment sized for 110 percent of the largest tank.
Provide a turbidimeter on the combined permeate of each train.
Provide a transmembrane pressure transmitter on each train.
Flow meters shall be magnetic flow meters with an accuracy of plus or minus 0.5 percent of rate.
Provide a programmable logic controller (PLC) control panel in a NEMA 12 enclosure for indoor installation.
The control panel shall communicate with the plant SCADA system over EtherNet/IP.
Provide an uninterruptible power supply that keeps the PLC running for not less than 30 minutes.
The control system shall automatically take a train out of production when transmembrane pressure exceeds the high setpoint.
The membrane system shall operate in automatic mode from the membrane system control panel and from the plant SCADA system.
In production mode the PLC shall adjust the permeate pump speed to hold each train at its flow setpoint.
Train flow setpoints shall follow the influent flow so that the membrane tank level stays within 6 inches of the level setpoint.
Relaxation or backpulse shall occur every 10 to 15 minutes, adjustable by the operator.
Air scour shall run continuously while a train is in production.
The PLC shall start a maintenance clean on each train at an interval set by the operator.
The PLC shall lock out a train in recovery clean mode until the operator confirms that the clean is complete.
High transmembrane pressure, low permeability, high permeate turbidity, and blower failure shall each generate an alarm at the control panel and at SCADA.
Alarm setpoints shall be adjustable from the operator interface without changes to the PLC program.
The operator interface shall trend flux, transmembrane pressure, permeability, and turbidity for each train for not less than 90 days.
Provide a color touchscreen operator interface not smaller than 15 inches on the control panel door.
Test the control panel at the factory with the final PLC program before shipment.
Notify the Engineer at least 21 days before the factory test of the control panel.
Permeate pumps shall be tested at the factory in accordance with ANSI/HI 14.6, acceptance grade 1B.
Air scour blowers shall be tested at the factory in accordance with ASME PTC 13.
Submit certified factory test reports before the equipment ships.
Shop prime and finish coat ferrous metal surfaces that will not be submerged.
Submerged components shall be stainless steel or plastic and shall not be painted.
Furnish spare membrane modules equal to 5 percent of the installed modules.
Furnish one spare permeate pump seal kit and one spare set of blower drive belts.
Verify that membrane tanks are clean and free of debris before installing cassettes.
Install cassettes level to within 0.25 inch across each cassette.
Do not install membrane modules until the tanks have been flushed and the band screens are in operation.
Perform a clean water test on each train to confirm permeate flow and transmembrane pressure before mixed liquor is introduced.
Clean water permeability shall be not less than 90 percent of the value stated in the process design report.
Perform a pressure decay test on each train before startup.
The pressure decay rate shall not exceed 0.5 psi in 10 minutes.
Repair or replace modules that fail the integrity test and retest the train.
Demonstrate every control mode, alarm, and interlock in the presence of the Engineer.
Demonstrate a maintenance clean and a recovery clean on one train.
Simulate a power failure and show that the system restarts in automatic mode when power returns.
Conduct a performance test of 30 days after the biological process has reached steady state.
During the test the system shall treat the design average flow with net flux and transmembrane pressure within the limits in Article 2.02.
Collect composite permeate samples three times per week for total phosphorus and TSS.
If the performance test fails, the Supplier shall modify the system and repeat the test at no cost to the Owner.
Seed the membrane tanks with mixed liquor from the existing plant under the direction of the manufacturer's representative.
Operate the system in manual mode for not less than 48 hours before switching to automatic control.
Provide operation and maintenance data for the membrane system in accordance with Section 01 33 00.
Provide a manufacturer's process engineer on site during the performance test.
Field service reports shall be submitted within 7 days after each visit.
Inspection of each membrane tank before cassettes are installed.
Inspection of the cassette installation and alignment.
Witnessing of the clean water test.
Calibration checks of the transmembrane pressure and turbidity instruments.
Verification of the PLC programming and alarm setpoints.
Supervision of the first maintenance clean.
The Contractor shall provide a factory-trained service technician on site for not less than 10 working days during startup.
Assistance with the performance test and the test report.
Provide not less than 16 hours of operator training on the membrane system in two sessions.
Training shall cover normal operation, cleaning procedures, membrane integrity testing, and troubleshooting.
Training sessions shall be video recorded and the recordings given to the Owner.
Spare membrane modules should be stored in the original shipping containers.
Membrane modules shall carry a full replacement warranty of 7 years from substantial completion.
Screen panels shall have perforations of 2 mm diameter.
